clue.text: Force to arrive long after Prince settles in

indicators.note: after says the long letter comes behind the rest, so it is placed at the end
the prince settles into the middle of the other letters, so this signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: A royal settling in somewhere compels people to turn up long afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles in' puts P inside COME, between M and E; 'after' sends L to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone is to oblige or push them into doing something.

clue.text: Gold and iron ring featured in opera

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A gold and iron ring appears as a prop in some opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Orfeo is Monteverdi's opera about the mythical singer Orpheus.

clue.text: A measure of a beating 20 you won't survive the end of?

definitions.text: A measure of a beating 20 you won't survive the end of?

parts.words: A measure of a beating 20 you won't survive the end of
parts.note: a reading of how fast a beating heart goes, a beat that stops only when life does

explanation.surface: Something is being measured that nobody outlives.
explanation.walkthrough: The '20' as held is a cross-reference to another light in the printed paper; the sense needed is the heart, whose beat is counted per minute and whose end is death.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical reading counts heartbeats per minute; when they end, so does life.

clue.text: Oxygen and carbon 22 found in recent spot

indicators.note: the two elements are found sitting inside the other word, so this signals a container

parts.note: something recent is late, as in 'the late news'
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Some oxygen and carbon have turned up recently at a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts OC inside LATE, after the L. The '22' as held is a cross-reference from the printed paper and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to find it, to pin down where it is.

clue.text: Company quotes without money rejected as superficial

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the cited word with its money is read backwards
without here means outside, so the quotes go round the money

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A firm turns down quotations that lack funding, calling them shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, making CITEMS, which 'rejected' turns to SMETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic change only touches the surface appearance and leaves the substance alone.

clue.text: Heartwarming quote from estate agent's blurb?

definitions.text: Heartwarming quote from estate agent's blurb?

parts.words: Heartwarming quote from estate agent's blurb
parts.note: a property advert phrase promising a warm house, read as warming at its core

explanation.surface: A touching line turns up in a house-selling advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartwarming' looks like 'touching', but it means warming the heart, the centre, of a home, as a house with a boiler in the middle is described in sales copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A house described this way is warmed throughout by a central boiler and radiators.

clue.text: No end of excessive passion in the cheapest berths

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: an excessive price is steep
rage is violent passion

explanation.surface: Unbounded passion breaks out in the cheap seats of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' takes the last letter from STEEP, leaving STEE.
explanation.definitionFit: On old passenger ships the lowest-priced accommodation was the deck section near the rudder.

clue.text: Rhine's seen rising round this German city

indicators.note: rising in a down clue says the hidden letters are read upwards, so backwards
the clue words go round the city, holding its letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A city on the Rhine is seen from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'round' into the definition, but 'round this German city' cannot stand in for a city name: 'round' says the words contain it, and 'rising' reads NESSE in 'rhiNE'S SEen' upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Lack of communication is round one initially engrossed by ancient language

parts.note: the letter O is round

indicators.note: engrossed by means held inside, so the letter goes into the language

parts.note: Latin is the language of ancient Rome

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in an old language is cut off from talking to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engrossed by' puts O, the first letter of 'one', inside LATIN, between I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off from others means no contact or exchange with them.

clue.text: Drinks supplier apparently refused permission?

explanation.surface: A shop selling drink seems to have been turned down for a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a licence that is 'off' has been withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop licensed to sell alcohol to take away; read literally, a permit switched off.

clue.text: Cries of delight resounding? Get away!

indicators.note: read as re-sounding, sounding back, so the cries are written backwards

parts.note: oohs are cries of delight

explanation.surface: Delighted shouts echo, and someone is told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resounding' looks like a sound clue, but it means sounding back: the cries are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an interjection used to drive off an animal or unwanted person.

clue.text: Here's guide lest road twists

indicators.note: the letters are twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: A guide is provided in case the road bends.
explanation.definitionFit: A star used for navigation, such as the Pole Star, leads the traveller.

clue.text: Subsequently backtracked about new hire charge

indicators.note: about here means around, so the backtracked word goes round the new letter
backtracked means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: subsequently means later

explanation.surface: Someone later goes back on a deal about a fresh charge for hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracked' turns LATER into RETAL, and 'about' wraps that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the fee paid for the use of a property or item for a period.

clue.text: Opera singer keen to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: keen means avid

explanation.surface: An eager prima donna wants to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female star of the opera house.

clue.text: I brewed tea with brine, being drunk

indicators.note: brewed means stewed up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone made tea with salt water, as only a drunk would.
explanation.walkthrough: The I stays at the front; 'brewed' mixes TEA and BRINE into NEBRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriate as an adjective means intoxicated, under the influence of alcohol.

clue.text: Face a set backing payment for lawyers

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock
to gel is to set, like a jelly

explanation.surface: Someone must face the task of financing a legal team.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAL + A + GEL reads DIALAGEL; 'backing' reverses the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: State funding that covers court costs for people unable to pay their own counsel.

clue.text: Treat Zola, ailing, in specialist hospital

indicators.note: ailing means in poor shape, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: The novelist Zola is ill and treated in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola is the French novelist Emile Zola; his name and TREAT are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazaretto was a quarantine hospital, especially for lepers or plague cases.

clue.text: Cover drive (in odd instances) getting scrambled single?

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled, so the letters are mixed into a new order
odd instances means the first, third and fifth letters of the word drive

explanation.surface: A cricket shot, the cover drive, goes wrong and only a single is scored.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'drive' are DIE; with COVER they are scrambled. A cover drive is a cricket stroke hit through the off side, and a single is one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorced person is single again after the marriage ends.

clue.text: Speed with which British will eschew fame

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the letter is left out

parts.note: celebrity is fame

explanation.surface: A British star will avoid fame quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness of movement or action.

clue.text: Metal and last of quartz included

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word quartz

parts.note: inc. is the short form of included or inclusive

explanation.surface: Some metal and a piece of quartz are part of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic element used in galvanising.

clue.text: Excess drugs and evidence of debts — very unpleasant

parts.note: OD is short for overdose, too much of a drug
IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Drug overdoses and piles of unpaid notes make for a grim life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful and repugnant.

clue.text: Shakespearean displaying nobility or vice and love

parts.note: a vice is a sin
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character shows either noble qualities or vice and love.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Twelfth Night, hence the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the lovesick Duke in Twelfth Night, a nobleman in the play.

clue.text: Covered with pen-marks? One's not covered, after article's erased

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: erased means rubbed out, so the letter goes from the word

parts.note: naked means not covered
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something is marked with ink, but one item is left bare after an essay is rubbed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erased' leaves NKED. 'Covered' in the definition plays against 'not covered' in the wordplay, and 'One's' is One has, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inked means marked with a pen, as in a signed or drawn-on page.

clue.text: Arrangement for older business in rich location

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word reorders its letters

parts.note: ado is fuss or business

explanation.surface: An older company makes plans in a wealthy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement for' makes ELDOR; El Dorado is Spanish for 'the gilded one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary South American city of gold, used for any place of riches.

clue.text: Urge King to enter gambling den

indicators.note: the king goes to enter the den, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or gambling den
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is urged to go into a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts R inside DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is an inner urge or motivation, as in a sex drive.

clue.text: Miss final snooker shot, abstracted at first?

indicators.note: abstracted means taken away, and at first says it is the opening letter

parts.note: in snooker the black is the last ball potted in a frame

explanation.surface: A player misses the deciding snooker shot, being distracted early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstracted' looks like 'absent-minded', but here it means removed: BLACK loses its first letter. Snooker is a billiards game in which the black ball is potted last.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to lack it, to be without it.

clue.text: Bunny rabbit represented 8 in cot a lot? About time

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the time letter
represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's toy bunny is shown in a cot quite a lot, for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN COT A LOT are rearranged around T. The '8' as held is a cross-reference from the printed paper and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The American wild rabbit is named for its white fluffy tail.

clue.text: Precisely the principal work in the garden

parts.note: dead means exactly, as in dead on time
the head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: The headteacher does some gardening, exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners remove faded flowers from plants to encourage more blooms.

clue.text: Cured, having adopted unhealthy lifestyle?

explanation.surface: Someone took up a bad habit, then gave it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cured meats and fish are preserved over wood smoke; the second reading is someone who took up cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish or ham preserved over a fire; also a person who once had a cigarette habit.
